comments.body:
**Verification and finalization of the proof.**

Verified the result symbolically (sympy solve over positive reals) and by numerical sampling. The system (E1)-(E4) has solution set exactly { x=y=z=1, t>0 }, i.e. (A,B,C,D)=(1,1,1,t^2). Sympy returns [{x:1,y:1,z:1}] with t free, matching the claimed answer.

The existing argument was already correct; I tightened it for full rigor: explicit necessity (Steps 1-4: x=y=z=1) and sufficiency (x=y=z=1, any t>0 is a solution) directions; every cancellation justified by positivity (each square is >0, hence nonzero/cancellable; u^2=1 with u>0 forces u=1 uniquely); noted (E2) reduces to (E1) (no extra info) and that t appears on both sides of (E4) so it is free; added a remark on why positivity is essential. No mathematical gap remains; the proof is complete and correct.
